summary: Today’s pulse tracks At least 2 deaths attributed to Isaias after hurricane bashes Florida and Alabama, Man dies after jumping into tiger enclosure at Yorkshire zoo, and Christa Pike out of hospital and back in prison after botched execution attempt. Across NPR, Guardian, and BBC, the strongest repeated signals are hurricane, isaias, and coast. In the background, Several injured in attack on airport in Saudi capital Riyadh and Hurricane Isaias live updates: warning of ‘spinoff tornadoes’ as hundreds of thousands without power keep the wider picture in motion.

headlines.title: At least 2 deaths attributed to Isaias after hurricane bashes Florida and Alabama
headlines.description: Hurricane Isaias is blamed for at least two deaths, after the storm made landfall on the Florida coast and ran through Alabama. The are numerous reports of downed trees, with hundreds of thousands of people without power.

headlines.title: Man dies after jumping into tiger enclosure at Yorkshire zoo
headlines.description: Police said man was pronounced dead at the scene after being attacked by tiger A man has died after being attacked by a tiger after jumping into its enclosure at a zoo in Yorkshire, police have said. Yorkshire Wildlife Park was evacuated shortly after the incident and the site will remain closed on Sunday.

headlines.title: Christa Pike out of hospital and back in prison after botched execution attempt
headlines.description: Pike’s lawyers said she is back in same prison she’s lived in for last 30 years and will continue to receive medical care Christa Pike has been discharged from the hospital after surviving Tennessee ’s botched 30 September attempt to execute her by lethal injection and is back in prison, her lawyers said on Saturday. Pike, 50, returned to the Deborah K Johnson rehabilitation center, where she has been imprisoned for the last three decades, her attorneys, Stephen Ferrell, Luke Ihnen, Randy Spivey and Kelly Gleason, said in a statement.

headlines.title: Several injured in attack on airport in Saudi capital Riyadh
headlines.description: The US embassy says it is "aware of attacks on King Khalid International Airport", which come days after Yemen's Houthis said they had struck it.

headlines.title: Hurricane Isaias live updates: warning of ‘spinoff tornadoes’ as hundreds of thousands without power
headlines.description: First Atlantic hurricane of the 2026 season makes landfall in the US Full story: Hurricane Isaias hammers Gulf coast Speaking to Fox News, he said: I think that may be a sign that people heeded the warnings, took proper precautions. We sure would love to say we have not gotten a report of a fatality yet, and we’ll see what happens. There’s also a lot of hazards post-storm that people should be careful of, but so far we’ve had a lot of assets in place that have not been called on, which is a good sign. I’d rather be over-prepared, and not have to use them, than not have what you need.” Hurricane Isaias has weakened to a post-tropical cyclone early Saturday, the National Hurricane Center (NHC) said, after it made landfall in Florida and lashed the US Gulf coast with heavy rain and fierce winds. The category 2 hurricane hit the coast near Destin, Florida, late on Friday, with maximum sustained winds of 105mph. The storm is expected to move across Alabama and into the Tennessee Valley, the NHC added, with maximum sustained winds decreased to near 35mph.

headlines.title: Thousands gather in London to express support for Palestinians after three years of ‘genocide’
headlines.description: Twenty arrested in first march since Ed Miliband declared UK’s position was that Israel’s occupation of West Bank was unlawful Thousands of people have gathered in central London to express their support for Palestinians after three years of “genocide” carried out against them by Israel. The demonstrators, many wearing keffiyehs and holding Palestine flags, gathered on the Embankment at midday on Saturday. Some carried placards reading “End the genocide” and “Free Palestine” as they marched towards parliament. A bride and groom appeared to be among those in attendance and a two-minute silence was held to reflect on the lives lost in Gaza.

headlinePool.title: US murderer Christa Pike discharged from hospital 10 days after failed execution
headlinePool.description: Pike's lawyers say she is "grateful" to the medical team who cared for her after she survived two lethal injections last month.

headlinePool.title: Dozens reported injured in Yemeni Houthi attack at Riyadh airport
headlinePool.description: Saudi authorities yet to confirm strike as government-allied forces in Yemen claim successful offensive to retake Bab al-Mandab strait Yemen’s Houthis have launched a missile attack on Riyadh’s international airport in Saudi Arabia, with dozens reported wounded and a witness describing panic in the terminal. Saudi authorities did not confirm any new attack or evacuation, but one witness reported hearing an explosion while waiting to board a flight, and another said they saw a strike that left people wounded.

headlinePool.title: Nine people, including children, dead after mass shooting in Pennsylvania
headlinePool.description: Authorities say suspect among dead in house after standoff with police in Erie and there is no ongoing threat Nine people, including children, died in a mass murder on Friday in Erie, Pennsylvania , after a gun-wielding attacker opened fire outside a home and then entered the property, according to authorities. The suspected attacker was also found dead as police responded to the deadly violence, which triggered a standoff involving Erie police officers and tactical teams.

headlinePool.title: Nobel peace laureate says US sanctions on ICC 'unacceptable'
headlinePool.description: Navi Pillay says the Trump administrations' sweeping penalties on the international tribunal were "unheard of".

headlinePool.title: Camden council was warned about paedophile nursery worker years before arrest
headlinePool.description: Vincent Chan went on to abuse children after being cleared of ‘significant concerns’ following council-overseen inquiry A paedophile nursery worker was cleared by an investigation overseen by a local authority three years before he was arrested. In February, Vincent Chan was jailed after pleading guilty to 56 offences , including assault by penetration on three-year-old girls in his care at a Bright Horizons nursery on Finchley Road in north-west London. After his conviction, prosecutors described him as a “prolific sexual predator”.

headlinePool.title: Woman injures three people in third Poland school knife attack in a week
headlinePool.description: Polish police had already deployed to schools after a female caretaker was killed and several others injured in two earlier attacks in two days.

headlinePool.title: Drone strike by Sudan paramilitary kills 41 near Ethiopian border, rights group says
headlinePool.description: Eight children are said to be among those killed by the strike, which hit a gathering of displaced people.

headlinePool.title: Ukraine hit by deadly Russian strikes as ‘thanks’ for Trump diesel deal, Zelenskyy says
headlinePool.description: Ukrainian president says money from fuel sales will intensify war as European leaders reiterate support for Kyiv Russia launched deadly strikes on civilians in Ukraine as “thanks” for a deal cut by Donald Trump with Vladimir Putin to buy large quantities of Russian diesel, Volodymyr Zelenskyy has said, accusing Washington of helping fund Moscow’s war. The Ukrainian president has expressed repeated outrage at the agreement announced by Trump on Friday, which the US president said was needed to reduce diesel prices, and comes ahead of November midterm elections in which fuel costs are a key voter issue.

headlinePool.title: Two dead as Isaias weakens to post-tropical cyclone after striking Florida panhandle
headlinePool.description: Deaths came from falling trees as nearly a million people are without power and rain and flooding remain a concern Two people have died amid Isaias after it made landfall late on Friday on Florida’s panhandle as a category 2 hurricane, according to authorities. Both of those deaths occurred after trees fell on homes, one in Escambia county, Florida, and another in Birmingham, Alabama, as the storm moved in inland, local officials said.
